standard_prerequisites.name: Differential graded module over a dg algebra
standard_prerequisites.statement: A graded A-module with a differential d of degree one satisfying the Leibniz rule, so that its cycles form a graded submodule.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the ambient category, and the two surjectivity clauses are statements about M and its cycles (source lines 2491-2500, 2512-2515).

standard_prerequisites.name: Admissible short exact sequence of dg modules
standard_prerequisites.statement: A short exact sequence of dg modules which splits as graded modules, so that the middle term is the direct sum of the outer terms.
standard_prerequisites.use: Clause (3) asks precisely for such a sequence with the outer terms direct sums of shifts of A, which is what the construction of P provides (source lines 2498-2500, 2510-2512).

standard_prerequisites.name: Shifted free module A[k]
standard_prerequisites.statement: The free dg A-module on one generator concentrated in degree k, with trivial differential.
standard_prerequisites.use: Adding direct sums of A[k] is how clause (2) is achieved without spoiling clause (3) (source lines 2512-2515).

core_obligations: Build the basic gadget: for each integer k let P_k be free on generators x and y in degrees k and k+1 with d(x) = y and d(y) = 0, and check that it is a dg A-module (source lines 2505-2507).

Produce the surjection and clause (3): for each element m of M of degree k use the map P_k -> M sending x to m and y to d(m), conclude that a direct sum of copies of the P_k surjects onto M, and observe that this P sits in an admissible short exact sequence with outer terms direct sums of shifts of A (source lines 2508-2512).

Upgrade to clause (2): for a cycle m of M of degree k use the map A[k] -> M sending 1 to m, and add a direct sum of copies of shifts of A to P to make Ker(d_P) -> Ker(d_M) surjective while keeping the admissible sequence (source lines 2512-2515).

proof_roadmap.step: Define the two-generator dg module P_k with d(x) = y and d(y) = 0.
Use maps P_k -> M to surject from a direct sum of copies of P_k, giving clauses (1) and (3).
Add direct sums of shifted copies of A so that the map on cycles is surjective, giving clause (2).

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-good-quotient at source lines 2489-2502: for a differential graded algebra A and any dg A-module M there is a homomorphism P -> M of dg A-modules which is surjective, whose restriction to the cycles Ker(d_P) -> Ker(d_M) is still surjective, and where P sits in an admissible short exact sequence with the outer terms direct sums of shifts of A. The proof at source lines 2504-2516 is a construction with a designed gadget rather than a citation: it builds the two-generator dg module P_k with generators in adjacent degrees k and k+1 and differential sending the first to the second, uses it to produce a surjection onto M from a direct sum of copies of P_k (which automatically gives the admissible short exact sequence of clause (3)), and then has to handle clause (2) separately by observing that a cycle of M of degree k admits a map from A[k] sending 1 to it, so that adding a direct sum of shifts of A upgrades the surjectivity on cycles. The piece that is doing the work is the gadget P_k and the fact that the added shifts do not disturb clause (3); the statement shows neither.
